teaser.text: Intuit sells software and expert help that let businesses keep books, move money, reach customers, and let people prepare taxes or choose financial products. Its business is a set of connected services, but its dollar flows differ: some customers pay Intuit directly, some partners pay for results, and much of the money passing through belongs to someone else.

stock.meta_description: Intuit stock forecast with weighted scenarios, the cash-flow test, key risks and the valuation behind the shares.
stock.opening: The weighted forecast is $318.88 in October 2027 and reaches $456.75 in October 2029. It hinges on paying-customer growth, ARPC, product attachment and retention moving together.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Intuit’s business works, who its rivals are, how management is executing, and where the risks sit.

blocks.heading: Where could Intuit's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted October 2027 price is $318.88, a 2% loss including dividends. It rises to $373.18, a 17% gain, in October 2028. At the final date it reaches $456.75, a 44% gain.
The final range runs from $180.64 to $801.45. Today’s price is $330.17. The bear case has a 30% probability, the base case 50%, and the bull case 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Intuit, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The outcome turns on paying-customer growth, ARPC, product attachment and retention moving together. AI and mid-market growth—businesses larger than small firms but smaller than large corporations—must show task accuracy, expert rework, service cost, paid adoption and retention, not usage alone. The October 2026 quarter is the first checkpoint; reporting is estimated for November 19, with revenue guided to $4,294–$4,313 million. Sequence’s October 15, 2026 acquisition agreement adds an integration and adoption test; its price was undisclosed. The thesis is durable cash generation from QuickBooks and assisted tax, not price, mix or tax timing alone.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Intuit really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation explains part of the gap. Intuit recorded $2,056 million of share-based compensation. It is added back because no cash leaves immediately, but employees still receive valuable ownership. Subtracting it from free cash flow leaves $6,561 million of “real free cash flow”, an owner-cost measure rather than a company-reported subtotal.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for Intuit?

paragraphs.text: At US$330.17 and a forward P/E of 14.4x, the implied future EPS is about US$22.93. That is close to management’s fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance of US$22.88–US$23.12. But Intuit now includes stock compensation in adjusted earnings, so comparisons with older adjusted figures are hazardous.

dividend.title: Intuit dividend: cash coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: Intuit dividend payments, cash coverage, forecast changes and yield against the share price.
dividend.opening: Intuit's current quarterly dividend is $1.38, or $5.52 annually, and the base forecast rises from $6.24 to $6.99 and then $7.83. Intuit's fiscal 2026 free cash flow of $8,617M covered $1,347M of dividends.
dividend.closing: The full Intuit memo also examines Intuit's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Intuit pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise in the base case because Intuit has increased them every year in the five-year record. The base starts at $6.24 and reaches $6.99. It ends at $7.83. The bear case holds the current quarterly rate at $1.38, or $5.52 annually, while the bull case maintains increases near the recent 15% pace. Fiscal 2026 free cash flow of $8,617M covered dividends of $1,347M, supporting the base path.

blocks.heading: Is Intuit's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Cash from operations was $8,838 million in fiscal 2026, against net income of $4,566 million. After $221 million of capital spending, conventional free cash flow was $8,617 million. Low capital spending does not mean the business is cheap to maintain: engineers, security, support and marketing are largely expensed through operations.

Stock compensation explains part of the gap. Intuit recorded $2,056 million of share-based compensation. It is added back because no cash leaves immediately, but employees still receive valuable ownership. Subtracting it from free cash flow leaves $6,561 million of “real free cash flow”, an owner-cost measure rather than a company-reported subtotal.
Working capital, payroll settlement and lending can also absorb cash. Dividends are therefore sustainable only if covered by repeatable cash after investment, compensation and financing needs.

earnings.title: Intuit earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Intuit expects results on November 19, 2026, with fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 9.0%–10.0% and customer growth as a key test.
earnings.opening: Intuit's next results are expected on November 19, 2026. Watch whether customer growth is genuine rather than driven by price, upgrades and accounting changes.
earnings.closing: The full memo also covers Intuit's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: What has Intuit guided for fiscal 2027?

paragraphs.text: Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance is $23,279–$23,512 million. That represents growth of 9.0%–10.0%, below fiscal 2026’s 14%. Global Business Solutions, which includes QuickBooks, is expected to grow 13.0%–14.0%. TurboTax is guided to 2.0%–3.0% growth, Credit Karma to 11.0%–13.0%, and Mailchimp to decline by 1.0% or remain flat.

Operating income is guided to grow 26.0%–27.0%, reaching a margin of about 32%. This is operating leverage: revenue grows, but costs grow more slowly. Imagine revenue rising by 10% while costs rise by less. Profit can then rise by 20%. The plan works only if savings are real and customer investment produces lasting revenue.

blocks.heading: Has Intuit kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: From August 2026, Intuit began including stock compensation in its adjusted financial measures. But its July 2024 expectation of growing headcount deserves scrutiny beside the May 2026 announcement of a 17% workforce reduction. The overall record is mixed: management has expertise and performance mechanisms, but owners must judge whether the AI bet, board oversight, insider behavior and changing promises ultimately serve them.

blocks.heading: How have Intuit's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: Revenue grew 13.7% year over year. Gross margin improved from 76.7% to 78.1%, and operating income rose from $339 million to $475 million. Net income and diluted EPS nevertheless fell, so the layers of the accounts were moving in different directions.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Intuit's next results?

paragraphs.text: The first checkpoint is the quarter ending October 2026, with reporting estimated for November 19. Management guides quarterly revenue to $4,294–$4,313 million. Adjusted earnings per share is guided to $2.44–$2.48. This is also the first quarter with the new compensation treatment and separate Mailchimp reporting, so comparability matters.
